title: Health-driven OTLP Export Gateway with Priority Fence and Adaptive Retry
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need a resilient OTLP export gateway that routes span traffic to multiple tracing backends (Tempo/Jaeger/third-party) using live backend health signals and tenant priorities. Current static fanout causes wasted tokenization, uneven load during backend flaps, and tail-latency spikes. This ticket builds a gateway component that: 1) continuously probes backend health and latency, 2) applies a per-tenant priority fence to favor higher-paying tenants and SLO-critical routes, 3) implements adaptive retry/circuit-breaker/backpressure and graceful fallback to a lower-cost sink (archival) when backends degrade.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway can route OTLP spans to at least two backends (Tempo and Jaeger) with a single configuration switch
Backend health metrics (latency, error rate, connection failures) are emitted to metrics pipeline and visible on the new dashboard
Per-tenant priority fence correctly prevents low-priority tenants from consuming >20% of a degraded backend's capacity
Adaptive retry respects per-backend circuit-breaker state and does not increase median latency for priority traffic by >25%
End-to-end tests cover failover from Tempo -> Jaeger and eventual archival to S3-compatible store
Runbook created and tested for manual remediation and rollback
design_decisions: Probe model: small synthetic span burst every 5s per backend + rolling latency percentiles; probe traffic tagged and excluded from billing
Routing policy: score = backend_health_score * tenant_priority_weight; use weighted least-latency with soft-fencing thresholds
Retries: exponential backoff with jitter up to 3 attempts for priority traffic; lower-priority traffic gets 0 retries when backend degraded
Circuit-breaker: per-backend and per-tenant windowed error-rate-based tripping with auto-recover after cooldown
Backpressure: in-memory per-backend queue with max_age and max_bytes; overflow triggers shed_to_archival policy
Data safety: spans sent to archival are encrypted at rest and flagged in metadata for retention reconciliation
rollout_plan: 1. Feature gated behind runtime-1.20 and feature flag observability.gateway.health_routing
2. Canary to 5% of tenant traffic in eu-west-1 for non-critical tenants for 48 hours
3. Measure failure rates and tail latency; abort canary if errors > 1% or p99 latency regression > 30%
4. Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% over 7 days with staggered tenant cohorts
5. Post-rollout monitoring: daily report for first week and SLA check at 30 days
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring function and priority fence
Integration test harness that spins up local Tempo and Jaeger mocks with configurable failure modes
Chaos test: simulate backend latency spikes and partial outages and validate failover correctness
Load test: verify per-backend queueing behaviour under 2x expected peak and ensure low-priority shedding occurs
E2E billing reconciliation test to ensure probe traffic and archival writes are not billed incorrectly
